flows.name: View landing page and get started
flows.goal: Understand what the app does and get started.

steps.userAction: The visitor opens the landing page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows what Solo Studio is for freelance client, project and booking management and how to start as designer or view public booking.

steps.userAction: The visitor chooses to get started as designer.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the designer sign-up page.

alternatives.condition: The visitor chooses to view public booking instead.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the public booking page with session types and open slots for the next two weeks.

alternatives.condition: The visitor already has an account and chooses to sign in.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the designer sign-in page.

flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; after refresh the landing page still shows the same explanation and start options.

flows.name: Designer sign up
flows.goal: Create an account and reach home.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to sign up.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty designer sign-up form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the sign-up form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website creates the isolated workspace, signs the designer in and shows home ready to add the first client.

alternatives.condition: The email is invalid or the password is shorter than 8 characters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.
The website says the email already has an account and offers to sign in instead.

alternatives.condition: The designer cancels without signing up.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is stored; the website shows the landing page as it was.

flows.outcome: A designer account exists and the designer is signed in; refresh still shows home.

flows.name: Designer sign in

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to sign in.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty designer sign-in form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the sign-in form and submits it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website verifies the credentials and shows home with today's sessions, follow-ups and overdue tasks.

alternatives.condition: The email or password is empty or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The email and password do not match an account.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the credentials are wrong and offers to try again.

flows.outcome: The designer is signed in; refresh still shows signed-in home.

flows.name: Designer sign out

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to sign out.
steps.websiteResponse: The website ends the session and shows the public landing page.

flows.outcome: The designer is signed out; refresh still shows the landing page.

flows.name: View home dashboard

steps.userAction: The designer opens home.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows today's sessions, follow-ups due this week including overdue, and overdue tasks with overdue highlight, each of which can be opened.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses a session, follow-up or overdue task to view.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the details of that session, client note or task.

alternatives.condition: There are no sessions today, no follow-ups due this week and no overdue tasks.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty home with guidance to add a first client and set availability.

alternatives.condition: The chosen session, note or task was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the item is gone and shows home again.

flows.outcome: Nothing is stored; refresh still shows the same today's sessions, follow-ups and overdue tasks.

flows.name: Add a client

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty client form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the client and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the client and shows its details with its follow-up state.

alternatives.condition: The name or email is empty or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.
Nothing is saved; the website shows the client list as it was.

flows.outcome: A new client is saved and still appears in the client list after refresh.

flows.name: View client list and edit client
flows.goal: Find a client and keep details current.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows clients with name, email, company, profile, status and follow-up state, sorted overdue follow-ups first then by earliest due date.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client details with its notes and projects.

steps.userAction: The designer edits the client details and saves them.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the changes and shows the updated client details.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty client list with guidance to add the first client.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.

alternatives.condition: The name or email is empty or invalid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the values and offers to retry.
Nothing is changed; the website shows the client details as they were.

alternatives.condition: The client has no notes or projects yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the client details with empty notes and projects sections and offers to add a first note or project.

flows.outcome: Client edits are saved and still shown after refresh with correct follow-up sorting.

flows.name: Delete a client
flows.goal: Remove a client and all its work.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client details with its notes, projects and bookings.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on the client.

alternatives.condition: The client was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the client is gone and shows the client list.
The website shows the client list without the client and without its projects, tasks, notes and bookings.
Nothing is deleted; the website shows the client again, unchanged.

flows.outcome: The client and its projects, tasks, notes and bookings are gone and stay gone after refresh.

flows.name: Manage notes and follow-ups
flows.goal: Track calls and never miss a follow-up.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the client list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows clients with name, company, status and follow-up state, overdue first.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the client details with dated notes and follow-up dates and done states.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a note.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty note form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the note and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the note with its creation date and shows it with the client notes and updated follow-up state.

steps.userAction: The designer marks a follow-up done or pushes it a week with one click.
steps.websiteResponse: The website updates the follow-up done state or moves the follow-up date a week later and updates the client list order.

steps.userAction: The designer edits a note and saves changes.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the note changes and shows the updated notes.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on a note.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no clients yet and offers to add one.

alternatives.condition: The client has no notes yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no notes yet and offers to add one.
The website marks the missing text and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website marks the missing text and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website shows the client notes without the deleted note.
The website shows the note again, unchanged.

flows.outcome: Notes and follow-up states are saved and still shown after refresh.

flows.name: Add and view projects
flows.goal: Organize work per client and see what is open.

steps.userAction: The designer opens projects.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all projects with their count of still-open tasks.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a client and chooses to add a project.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty project form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the project and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the project and shows it in the projects list with zero open tasks.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a project from the list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the project details with its tasks.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no projects yet and offers to add one under a client.

alternatives.condition: Required project name or description is missing.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is missing and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: The project has no tasks yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the project details with zero open tasks and offers to add a task.

alternatives.condition: The project was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the project is gone and shows the projects list.

flows.outcome: New projects are saved with correct open-task counts and still shown after refresh.

flows.name: Edit and delete a project
flows.goal: Keep projects correct or remove them.

steps.userAction: The designer opens projects.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all projects with their count of still-open tasks.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a project.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the project name, description and due date with its tasks.

steps.userAction: The designer edits the project and saves changes.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the changes and shows the updated project.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on the project.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no projects yet and offers to add one.

alternatives.condition: The project was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the project is gone and shows the projects list.

alternatives.condition: Required project name or description is missing.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is missing and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website shows the projects list without the deleted project and its tasks.
The website shows the project again, unchanged.

flows.outcome: Project edits are saved or the project with its tasks is gone; both persist after refresh.

flows.name: Manage tasks in a project
flows.goal: Track and complete project work quickly.

steps.userAction: The designer opens projects.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows all projects with their count of still-open tasks.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a project.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the project tasks with title, status, priority and due date, with overdue tasks highlighted.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to add a task.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows an empty task form.

steps.userAction: The designer fills in the task and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the task and shows it in the task list with updated open counts.

steps.userAction: The designer searches by title and filters by status and priority.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows only the tasks matching the search and filters.

steps.userAction: The designer ticks a task done.
steps.websiteResponse: The website sets the task status to Done, removes its overdue highlight and updates the open count.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no projects yet and offers to add one.

alternatives.condition: The project has no tasks yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no tasks yet and offers to add one.
The website marks the missing title and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: No tasks match the search or filters.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that nothing matches and offers to clear the search and filters.

alternatives.condition: The project was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the project is gone and shows the projects list.

flows.outcome: Tasks and their done states are saved with correct filters and highlights after refresh.

steps.userAction: The designer opens the project task list.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the project tasks with overdue highlight.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a task.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the task title, status, priority and due date.

steps.userAction: The designer edits the task and saves changes.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the changes and shows the updated task with correct overdue highlight.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on the task.

alternatives.condition: The task was deleted in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the task is gone and shows the project task list.
The website marks the missing title and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

flows.outcome: Task edits are saved or the task is gone; both persist after refresh.

flows.name: Set availability and session types
flows.goal: Define when and what visitors can book.

steps.userAction: The designer opens scheduling settings.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the current weekly availability and the session types with duration, display-only price and maximum people.

steps.userAction: The designer sets weekly availability and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the available days and start and end times for generating the next two weeks of slots.

steps.userAction: The designer creates a session type and saves it.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the session type and shows it with the other types.

steps.userAction: The designer edits a session type and saves changes.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the changes and shows the updated session type.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses Delete on a session type.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that no availability is set yet and offers to set weekly days and times.

alternatives.condition: Days are missing or the end time is not after the start time.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: Required session type fields are missing or numbers are out of range.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.

alternatives.condition: Required session type fields are missing or numbers are out of range.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website shows the session types without the deleted type.
The website shows the session type again, unchanged.

flows.outcome: Availability and session types are saved and still shown after refresh.

flows.name: View upcoming sessions and cancel a slot
flows.goal: Manage upcoming bookings and cancel when needed.

steps.userAction: The designer opens upcoming sessions.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows upcoming sessions with session type, time, booking count and booker names.

steps.userAction: The designer opens a session.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the session details with everyone booked on it.

steps.userAction: The designer chooses to cancel the slot.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that there are no upcoming sessions and offers to set availability and session types.

alternatives.condition: The session was cancelled in the meantime.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the session is gone and shows the upcoming sessions list.
The website shows the upcoming sessions without the cancelled slot and its bookings.
The website shows the session again, unchanged.

alternatives.condition: The session has no bookings yet.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows the session details with no bookings yet and offers to cancel the slot or go back.

flows.outcome: Cancelled slots and their bookings are gone and stay gone after refresh.

flows.name: Book a session from public page
flows.goal: Book a session without an account.

steps.userAction: The booker opens the public booking page.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the session types with duration, display-only price and seats per slot.

steps.userAction: The booker picks a session type.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows open slots for the next two weeks for that type, excluding past times and full slots.

steps.userAction: The booker chooses a slot and books with name and email.
steps.websiteResponse: The website saves the booking under the matching client or a new Lead client and shows a confirmation with a cancellation link.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that no sessions are offered right now and offers to try again later.

alternatives.condition: There are no open slots for the chosen type in the next two weeks.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website shows that nothing is open for that type and offers to pick another session type.

alternatives.condition: Name or email is missing or the email is not valid.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website marks what is wrong and keeps what was typed.
The website keeps the typed values and offers to retry.
The website says the slot is now full and offers to pick another open slot.

flows.outcome: A booking and its linked Lead or existing client are saved; the confirmation with cancellation link is shown and the slot shows one fewer open seat after refresh.

flows.name: Cancel a booking via link
flows.goal: Cancel a booking via link without an account.
preconditions: A booking with a valid cancellation link exists.

steps.userAction: The booker opens the cancellation link.
steps.websiteResponse: The website shows the booking details with session type, date and time and booker name, with an option to cancel.

steps.userAction: The booker chooses to cancel the booking.

alternatives.condition: The link is invalid or the booking was already cancelled.
alternatives.websiteResponse: The website says the booking cannot be found and shows how to make a new booking.
The website shows the booking is cancelled, the seat is open again and the client record is kept.

alternatives.condition: The booker does not confirm the cancellation.
alternatives.websiteResponse: Nothing is cancelled; the website shows the booking again unchanged.

flows.outcome: The booking is gone and the slot is open again after refresh; the client remains.

fields.label: Designer email
fields.meaning: Email the designer uses to sign up and sign in

fields.label: Designer password
fields.meaning: Secret password protecting the designer's workspace

fields.label: Client name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the client

fields.label: Client email
fields.meaning: Email used to contact the client and to link bookings

fields.label: Client company
fields.meaning: Optional company the client belongs to

fields.label: Client profile
fields.meaning: Short note about what they do, how met and what they pay
fields.example: Runs a D2C skincare brand, met at Design Day, pays per milestone

fields.label: Client status
fields.meaning: Where the client is in the pipeline

fields.label: Note text
fields.meaning: What was discussed or remembered after a call
fields.example: Call about checkout redesign, wants proposal by Friday

fields.label: Follow-up date
fields.meaning: Optional date to follow up on this note

fields.label: Project name
fields.meaning: How the designer refers to the work for a client

fields.label: Project description
fields.meaning: Short summary of what the project covers
fields.example: Simplify checkout to 2 steps and improve mobile conversion

fields.label: Project due date
fields.meaning: Optional date the project should be finished by

fields.label: Task title
fields.meaning: What needs to be done in the project

fields.label: Task status
fields.meaning: Where the task is in its workflow

fields.label: Task priority
fields.meaning: How urgent the task is

fields.label: Task due date
fields.meaning: Optional date the task should be done by, overdue when past and not Done

fields.label: Available days
fields.meaning: Which weekdays repeat weekly as bookable

fields.label: Available from time
fields.meaning: Start of the bookable window on available days

fields.label: Available to time
fields.meaning: End of the bookable window on available days

fields.label: Session type name
fields.meaning: Name of the bookable offering shown to visitors

fields.label: Session type duration
fields.meaning: Length in minutes used to slice availability into slots

fields.label: Session type price display
fields.meaning: Display-only price text shown on booking, never charged

fields.label: Session type maximum people
fields.meaning: How many bookings a slot holds before it is full

fields.label: Booker name
fields.meaning: Name of the visitor booking a session

fields.label: Booker email
fields.meaning: Email of the visitor, used to link to an existing client or create a Lead

fields.label: Chosen session type
fields.meaning: Which offering the visitor wants to book

fields.label: Chosen slot
fields.meaning: Which open time slot the visitor books

fields.label: Task search query
fields.meaning: Free text to find tasks by title

fields.label: Task status filter
fields.meaning: Show only tasks with this status

fields.label: Task priority filter
fields.meaning: Show only tasks with this priority

steps.websiteResponse: The website asks to confirm the deletion and says what else will be removed with it.

alternatives.websiteResponse: The website deletes the record and what belongs to it.
Nothing is deleted; the record stays as it was.

assumptions.text: Notes can be edited and deleted by the designer; deleting a note removes its follow-up; marking done or pushing a week never deletes the note.

Sessions are not manually created; upcoming sessions are weekly availability sliced into back-to-back slots per session type duration for the next two weeks; the designer manages them only by viewing and cancelling, with each session showing booking count and booker names.
